transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-06-11 11:00 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CISO, Silverpine), Tomás Rivera (Head of Platform), Nina Okoye (Infra), Ravi Menon (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood ran a deep dive into private/VPC/on-prem security architecture. Focus areas: egress gateway design, network isolation, firewalling and port allowlists, RBAC and SSO integration options, audit log retention and data residency, and KMS/BYOK. Customer shared constraints: must keep all PHI in-region, SOC2 + ISO required, BYOK preferred but evaluating HSM options. Next steps and action items captured.

Topics: egress gateway architecture; VPC peering vs PrivateLink; NAT vs managed egress proxies; egress filtering and DLP; RBAC/SSO (SAML/SCIM); audit log collection and retention; KMS integration (BYOK/HSM); SOC2/ISO evidence pack; pilot plan and soak tests.

Action items (captured in notes): see metadata.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. quick check on attendees?
[00:06] Tomás Rivera: Tomás here, Nina and Ravi and Lena on my side.
[00:09] Lena Ortiz: Hey, Lena, CISO.
[00:11] Arjun Patel: Arjun from Redwood, I'll be the SE on this call.
[00:14] Maya Chen: Great. We printed the agenda in the calendar but we'll hop into your high level constraints first, Lena, you want to share?
[00:22] Lena Ortiz: Sure. We're Silverpine Medical, we have to keep PHI in-region so all inference and logs must remain in US-east-1. We're SOC2 in progress, ISO27001 in the checklist. Main questions: can Redwood run inside our VPC or on-prem, what are the egress controls, how does KMS BYOK work, and how do we get audit logs to our Splunk cluster, also RBAC and SSO integration.
[00:42] Arjun Patel: ok got it. so for Private deployment we support a customer-controlled plane where the inference runtime sits in your VPC or on-prem VM pools. There is a private control plane option and a fully offline package for air-gapped installs. now on the network side, for egress we typically recommend a dedicated egress gateway - either a managed HA egress proxy inside the VPC or a passthrough to your existing egress appliance.
[01:06] Tomás Rivera: can you clarify what you mean by managed HA? do you mean Redwood runs a proxy inside our subnet that we manage?
[01:12] Arjun Patel: yeah, so two patterns: (1) Redwood-deployed egress proxy container that you host in your subnet behind your firewall, we give a docker image and config; or (2) we route outbound traffic via your corporate egress appliance using NAT rules and we provide a signed cert for mTLS to authenticate to Redwood control plane if needed. in both cases we can enforce allow-lists by CIDR and FQDN.
[01:37] Nina Okoye: is there a difference for KV cache and model downloads? we want to make sure large model pulls don't leak to public buckets.
[01:43] Arjun Patel: good point. model artifacts are pulled during initial provisioning — we support pulling from our artifact storage over private link endpoints or via an s3 bucket replicant. you can also mirror models to your internal object store; we have a recommended sync tool. the egress rules will need outbound to the artifact endpoint IPs or to AWS PrivateLink endpoints.
[02:02] Ravi Menon: BYOK is critical. we require customer-managed keys in an HSM. does Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM providers?
[02:09] Arjun Patel: yes — we integrate with customer KMS through standard APIs. for AWS we support KMS CMKs and can integrate with CloudHSM for HSM-backed keys. for on-prem we support a PKCS#11 interface to HSMs and can mount a keywrap. caveat: some workflows, like model snapshot encryption, need key wrapping handshake that we can do in-tenant.
[02:30] Lena Ortiz: and key rotation? we need quarterly rotations with zero downtime.
[02:34] Arjun Patel: we support key rotation with rolling crypto keys and rewrap; for long lived caches we re-encrypt on rotation. it's an ops flow we document. we should get details from your KMS team about their rotation windows.
[02:46] Maya Chen: quick interruption — SOC2 evidence: we can share our SOC2 Type II report and an ISO attestation. I'll send that after the call.
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: please. also a compliance mapping to our controls would help.
[02:57] Maya Chen: noted.
[03:00] [03:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:04] Arjun Patel: back to network: for strict egress filtering we propose two things: an egress gateway with allowlist at the FQDN level plus TLS inspection for DLP, or an egress-only NAT with proxy chaining into your DLP appliance. which of these aligns with your stack?
[03:23] Tomás Rivera: we have a Zscaler/cloud egress proxy right now but it's a shared-prod appliance. would you prefer a dedicated egress vm?
[03:30] Arjun Patel: dedicated egress VM gives you better isolation and easier auditing — you can collect per-container logs, rotate certs. if you want to keep Zscaler, we can integrate via proxy chaining, but that makes granular per-tenant observability harder.
[03:44] Nina Okoye: for audit logs — we need 7 years retention for certain events. can Redwood forward audit logs to our Splunk indexer and do log redaction?
[03:54] Arjun Patel: yes. we support syslog/HTTPS push to SIEMs, and we have configurable PII redaction filters. default retention on our side is 90 days, but in Private deployments you control retention and ship logs to your collector for archive.
[04:10] Lena Ortiz: what about data residency — any replication outside the region?
[04:13] Arjun Patel: no replication if you choose dedicated private mode and pin to us-east-1. Hosted mode might replicate across regions for HA, but Private/VPC you can pin and we won't replicate.
[04:22] Ravi Menon: network segmentation: we want separate subnets for runtime, model storage, and the egress gateway, with firewall rules blocking east-west traffic except through a vetted service mesh. supported?
[04:34] Arjun Patel: yes — typical deployment uses three subnets: control plane (management), runtime (inference), and artifacts. We recommend no direct inbound to runtime from internet; all ingress via load balancer with IP allowlist or private link. East-west enforced via security groups + service mesh mTLS.
[04:53] Maya Chen: quick note: our runtime supports mutual TLS between components — we rotate certs via Vault or your KMS.
[04:59] Tomás Rivera: speaking of certs, does Redwood require a pinned cert to reach the control plane or do you support client cert rotation?
[05:05] Arjun Patel: we support both. for high security customers we do mTLS with client certs stored in your vault. we can accept a CA you control.
[05:13] [05:13] Speaker 2: mm hmm
[05:15] Nina Okoye: about RBAC and SSO — we use Okta and want SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO with groups mapped to roles. does Redwood support granular RBAC per model/route?
[05:26] Arjun Patel: yes, Redwood's console supports roles at multiple levels: org, project, model route. we sync via SCIM and accept group claims from SAML, and also have attribute-based access policies. small gotcha: some legacy onboard flows may need manual role mapping if you have custom claims.
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: audit trails are critical. we need immutable logs of who called what API, token-level traces, and ability to export to our retention store.
[05:52] Arjun Patel: we capture token-level traces and per-request metadata — timestamps, caller identity, route, model version, latency, truncated content hashes. these can be pushed to your SIEM or stored in your S3 for long term. note: request payloads with PHI must be redacted if policies require.
[06:11] Tomás Rivera: performance question — if we put an egress gateway that inspects TLS for DLP it might add 30-100ms per request. does Redwood support local caching to reduce roundtrips?
[06:20] Arjun Patel: yes, we have a local KV cache on the runtime so repeated prefixes don't hit external artifact endpoints or do extra egress. batching also reduces total egress calls.
[06:29] Ravi Menon: can we do split tunneling so only artifact and telemetry go out but model inference stays internal?
[06:34] Arjun Patel: inference is internal; telemetry and model artifact downloads are the main egress. you can route telemetry to internal endpoints via private link. artifact mirrors solve the rest.
[06:44] [06:44] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[06:47] Maya Chen: let's get a bit more specific — Arjun, sketch an initial network ACL and ports we need to allow for the pilot.
[06:53] Arjun Patel: sure. at minimum: outbound 443 to artifact endpoints (private link IPs), outbound 443 to control plane for health checks if using private control plane (mTLS), outbound 443 to your SIEM/metrics endpoints, and if you use image pull registries you'll need access to container registry endpoints. If you need agent updates we recommend allowing TLS to our update endpoint — but for air-gapped we'll provide bundles.
[07:16] Nina Okoye: what about inter-subnet security group rules? we want no broad 0.0.0.0/0 egress from runtime.
[07:21] Arjun Patel: absolutely — runtime should be locked down to only allow egress to the artifact and telemetry endpoints and to the egress gateway. no inbound from internet.
[07:29] Lena Ortiz: compliance: we run periodic pen tests and need to include Redwood in our third party pen test scope. is that ok?
[07:36] Arjun Patel: yes, we have a third-party pentest policy. for Private deployments we can coordinate a scoping call; we do require a nondisclosure and test windows. we'll provide our testing guide.
[07:48] Maya Chen: question from my side: do you have retention windows for logs that are acceptable, or specific legal retention tied to PHI?
[07:55] Lena Ortiz: we have to comply with HIPAA-ish guidelines — not strictly HIPAA but similar. we want seven years for audit events and three years for access logs at least.
[08:03] Arjun Patel: we'll push logs to your S3 and you can lifecycle them. we can also support server-side encryption with your CMK.
[08:11] [08:11] Speaker 3: uh-huh
[08:13] Tomás Rivera: cost question — does dedicated egress VM meaningfully add to monthly costs?
[08:17] Maya Chen: typically it's a small infra cost relative to GPUs, but depends on throughput.
[08:23] Arjun Patel: yes and we can rightsize. part of Redwood Optimize is a sizing guide and recommended batching which can reduce egress and overall network cost.
[08:31] Nina Okoye: about HSM integrations — we use Thales Luna. has Redwood done Luna integrations before?
[08:36] Arjun Patel: we've integrated Thales and AWS CloudHSM. for Thales we'd do PKCS#11 and a keywrap. it's a bit more ops work but doable. we'll need credentials and an air-gapped test rotation cycle.
[08:52] Lena Ortiz: are there any default logs that Redwood collects which we can't disable?
[08:56] Arjun Patel: default telemetry includes health and runtime metrics and error traces. request payload logging is opt-in and can be redacted. you control what we persist locally versus ship out.
[09:06] [09:06] Speaker 2: okay
[09:08] Maya Chen: let's discuss a sample pilot: 2-week pilot, pinned to us-east-1, mirror models to your internal s3, dedicated egress VM, SCIM/Okta SSO, forward logs to your Splunk — success criteria: no egress outside region, keys managed by customer, <100ms added latency for inference P95. thoughts?
[09:30] Lena Ortiz: sounds reasonable. add a security soak where we run a small pen test and audit logs and cert rotation.
[09:36] Ravi Menon: and we'll run throughput tests to ensure the egress VM doesn't become a bottleneck.
[09:41] Arjun Patel: we'll provide a benchmark harness and tooling. we'll also provide a traffic generator to validate throughput.
[09:49] Tomás Rivera: on the SSO front, we need SCIM group mapping to roles and audit webhook to notify of provisioning changes.
[09:56] Arjun Patel: we have SCIM provisioning and webhooks; we'll share the schema.
[10:01] [10:01] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[10:04] Maya Chen: any blockers we haven't covered?
[10:06] Nina Okoye: just one — encryption in transit between runtime pods and model store; is that mTLS?
[10:11] Arjun Patel: yes all internal component traffic uses mutual TLS. keys can be supplied from your Vault.
[10:16] Lena Ortiz: regulatory question: will Redwood sign Business Associate Agreement or similar?
[10:21] Maya Chen: yes, for PHI we can engage legal and our BAA template. we'll loop in legal in the next step.
[10:27] Ravi Menon: about firewalling — do you have a recommended default deny strategy?
[10:31] Arjun Patel: default deny is our recommendation. use security groups with least privilege, only allow egress to specific endpoints, and use egress gateway for DLP.
[10:40] [10:40] Speaker 2: mm
[10:42] Maya Chen: Ok let's recap next steps. Arjun you'll draft the egress rule template and network diagram; I'll send SOC2/ISO docs and legal will follow up on BAA. Silverpine will send firewall rules and confirm BYOK requirement. We agreed to schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-06-29 pending deliverables.
[10:58] Lena Ortiz: yep. Please include expected latency hit numbers for DLP-enabled egress VM in the diagram.
[11:04] Arjun Patel: will do — I'll include conservative numbers and optimization options.
[11:08] Tomás Rivera: one more ask — can you include a runbook for certificate rotation and emergency key revoke?
[11:14] Arjun Patel: yes, I'll add a runbook and an ops playbook for key compromise.
[11:18] Maya Chen: awesome. thanks for a productive session. we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[11:22] [11:22] Meeting ends

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings around product names (e.g., 'Private control plane' may appear as 'private control plain'), technical acronyms such as PKCS#11, HSM, SCIM may be mis-capitalized or hyphenated incorrectly. There may be short inaudible segments marked in-line.
